correctness.rationale: A degree-profile bijection shows that a selected pair of degree-one vertices has a common center with probability sum_v(t_v)_2/(N)_2. Conditional on k distinct symbols in a length-N Prüfer word, equal contents at two designated positions have probability S(N-1,k)/S(N,k). A proof of real-rootedness for Stirling polynomials using B_{m+1}=z(B_m+B_m') yields coefficient log-concavity and strictly decreasing ratios in k, including endpoint k=N; thus the regression strictly rises with leaf count. The likelihood-ratio tilt and strictly positive covariance for any nonconstant nondecreasing f follow by conditional expectation and the independent-copy identity. All 280388 enumerated trees and 4850 finite monotonicity checks pass in standalone exact arithmetic.

The earliest full texts inspected establish only the leaf marginal (Rényi 1959), unconditioned cherry moments (Erdős–Rényi 1963), or general degree-profile enumeration (Pitman 1997); the 2020 cherry result counts a narrower statistic. value.rationale: Leaf-twin pairs encode local graph automorphisms, whereas leaf count is a global tree-shape statistic. The exact two-leaf contraction gives a Palm construction whose leaf-count law is a precise empty-box distribution. The complete exact conditional regression provides a genuine statistical ordering: conditioning by local symmetry witnesses shifts the leaf distribution in strict monotone likelihood-ratio order at every size, and forces positive covariance with every increasing nonconstant leaf statistic. This distributional structure is not a trivial count, and is stronger than the classical unconditional cherry expectation or leaf marginal.
